narrative.overview:
The site is a letter from the family in Dadagaun to a friend abroad. It opens with "Dear friend," and closes with a reply slip. Everything is built from the objects of international post: thin blue airmail paper, the red and navy chevron border, perforated stamps, rubber postmarks and franking-meter numerals. Those objects carry real content. The children's photo is printed as the stamp, the founding year is the postmark, and the approved figures are franked in red.

The page is calm and plainly honest, because its reader is a stranger deciding whether to trust a children's home with money. Postal ornament appears only at the moments a letter would carry it, and everything else is ruled paper and good type.
keyCharacteristics: Cool airmail-blue ground, never warm cream.
A wide grotesque speaks in postal labels and headlines; a reading serif carries the letter voice.
Ruled lines and negative space instead of cards.
One primary action per view, in airmail red.

rules.name: The Chevron Rule
rules.body: The red and navy chevron frames only letter moments: the hero letter sheet, the reply slip and the "Write to us" form, plus the footer's top edge. It is never used as a divider or a decorative stripe elsewhere.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is navy ink, never gray or black. Secondary text on a navy section uses the sheet colour at reduced opacity, not gray.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the post office: labels, headlines, numbers, controls. Literata is the family writing: everything said in sentences. A paragraph is never set in Archivo.

dos: Do let real content carry the postal objects: photos as stamps, years as postmarks, figures as franking.
Do keep claims to the approved figures in PRODUCT.md and derive nothing new.
Do use ruled lists and two-column splits instead of card grids.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: the postmark and digit roll settle instantly.
donts: Don't use eyebrow labels above headings, or em dashes anywhere in copy.
Don't spread the chevron border or postmarks onto every section; they mark letter moments only.
Don't use warm cream, gray text or pure black.
Don't set the full-bleed dimmed-photo hero with a stat bar and three icon cards that this site replaced.
